intro: Some pieces of the Great Altar never went to Berlin, and this is where they wait for you. Bergama Museum, in İzmir province, opened in 1936, and it holds the finds from the acropolis, the Asklepion and the Red Basilica.
history: The museum opened in 1936 to hold what remained in Türkiye from a century of excavation at Pergamon. Alongside finds from the acropolis, the Asklepion, the Red Basilica and the tumuli around them, it also keeps an ethnographic collection from the town's Ottoman centuries.
highlights: As you wander through the halls, don't miss the Sculpture hall, the finds from the Asklepion, the fragments of the Great Altar and the Ethnography hall.
facts: Did you know? The great frieze of the Altar of Zeus went to Berlin in the nineteenth century, so the fragments kept here are the only original part of it that you can see in Bergama. The collection also includes the votive objects found in the healing centre of the Asklepion.
outro: This brings our tour of Bergama Museum to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash. These pieces have come a long way to reach you; let them tell their story to those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
